title: MockBackend.new_with_account vs MemoryBackend.new_with_accounts (plural, slice) is inconsistent — the same kind of constructor on two adjacent backends with different parameter shapes
description:
What is awkward: lib.rs:194 MockBackend::new_with_account(account_id: &str) takes one account by name. memory.rs:283 MemoryBackend::new_with_accounts(account_ids: &[&str]) takes a slice. Same conceptual operation, different shapes.

This is a small papercut but compounds: every test that uses both backends has to remember which constructor takes a single name vs a slice. Tests in tests/metadata_tests.rs use new_with_accounts(&["acc1"]); tests in metadata.rs::tests use new_with_account("acc1"). The mock-vs-memory distinction creates two parallel test idioms.

Fix: align on one shape. The slice form is strictly more general, so MockBackend::new_with_account could become new_with_accounts(&[name]) at the call sites. Or add new_with_account convenience to MemoryBackend. Either way, ONE shape on both.
